stem.en: Which is NOT one of the components of data communication?

explanation.en: The components are sender, receiver, message, communication medium and protocols. A compiler is a program translator.

stem.en: The set of rules that sender and receiver follow while communicating is called a:

explanation.en: Protocols define the format, timing and sequence of data exchange.

stem.en: Bandwidth of a channel is measured in:

explanation.en: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies (highest − lowest) a channel can carry, measured in Hz, kHz, MHz, GHz.

stem.en: A telephone voice channel carries frequencies from 300 Hz to 3400 Hz. Its bandwidth is:

explanation.en: Bandwidth = highest − lowest frequency = 3400 − 300 = 3100 Hz.

stem.en: How long does it take to transfer a 500 MB file over a link with a data transfer rate of 40 Mbps (ignore overheads)?

explanation.en: 500 MB = 500 × 8 = 4000 Mb (megabits). Time = 4000 / 40 = 100 s. Remember B = byte = 8 bits.

stem.en: Communication between a walkie-talkie pair, where only one person can talk at a time, is:

explanation.en: Both sides can send, but not at the same time: half-duplex.

stem.en: Which of these is an example of simplex communication?

options.en: Data sent from a keyboard to the computer

explanation.en: In simplex, data flows only one way, as from a keyboard to the CPU or from a radio station to listeners.

stem.en: In which switching technique is a dedicated path set up between sender and receiver before communication starts?

explanation.en: Traditional telephone calls use circuit switching: the path is reserved for the whole call.

stem.en: Which statement about packet switching is correct?

options.en: Data is never broken into smaller pieces
It is used only for analog voice calls
Packets of the same message may take different routes and are reassembled at the destination
A dedicated path is reserved for the whole session

explanation.en: In packet switching each packet is routed independently; no dedicated path is reserved, so the links are shared efficiently.

stem.en: A video call where both people speak and hear each other at the same time is:

explanation.en: Simultaneous two-way communication is full-duplex.

stem.en: Which wired medium carries data as light pulses?

explanation.en: Optical fibre carries light through a glass or plastic core by total internal reflection.

stem.en: The cable commonly used for cable TV connections, with a central copper conductor surrounded by insulation and a braided metal shield, is:

explanation.en: Coaxial cable has a copper core, an insulating layer, a braided shield and an outer cover.

stem.en: Wires in a twisted pair cable are twisted to:

options.en: Increase the length of the wire

explanation.en: Twisting cancels much of the noise picked up from outside and between pairs (crosstalk).

stem.en: Which is an advantage of optical fibre over copper cables?

options.en: It is the cheapest and easiest to install
It can be bent sharply without damage
It is immune to electromagnetic interference and has very high bandwidth

explanation.en: Light is not affected by electrical noise, and fibre supports very high data rates over long distances. It is costlier and fragile.

stem.en: In an optical fibre, light stays inside the core because:

options.en: The core has a higher refractive index than the cladding, giving total internal reflection
The cladding is made of copper
Light travels only in straight lines in glass

explanation.en: The core (higher refractive index) and cladding (lower) cause total internal reflection, guiding light along the fibre.

stem.en: A TV remote control uses which type of waves?

explanation.en: Infrared is used for very short, line-of-sight communication and cannot pass through walls.

stem.en: Which waves are omnidirectional and can pass through walls, making them suitable for AM/FM radio?

explanation.en: Radio waves (about 3 kHz to 1 GHz) spread in all directions and can penetrate walls.

stem.en: Which waves need line of sight and are used for satellite and point-to-point links between towers?

explanation.en: Microwaves (about 1–300 GHz) travel in straight lines and are unidirectional; the antennas must face each other.

stem.en: Bluetooth is used for:

options.en: Short-range wireless connection of personal devices

explanation.en: Bluetooth connects devices within about 10 m and forms a PAN (piconet).

stem.en: Arrange in increasing order of frequency: microwaves, infrared, radio waves.

explanation.en: Radio ≈ 3 kHz–1 GHz, microwaves ≈ 1–300 GHz, infrared ≈ 300 GHz–400 THz.

stem.en: Which generation of mobile technology was analog and supported only voice calls?

explanation.en: 1G (1980s) used analog signals for voice only.

stem.en: SMS (text messaging) became possible with:

explanation.en: 2G introduced digital communication and services like SMS and MMS.

stem.en: Which generation is known for very high speed, very low latency and support for massive IoT connections?

explanation.en: 5G is designed for high data rates, low latency and connecting a very large number of devices.

stem.en: Mobile Internet browsing and video calling first became practical with:

explanation.en: 3G offered higher data speeds, enabling mobile Internet and video calls.

stem.en: Which is the correct match?

options.en: 4G – LTE, high-speed data for HD video streaming

explanation.en: 4G (LTE) gave high-speed mobile broadband; 1G was analog voice, 2G digital with SMS.

stem.en: Which protocol is used to send e-mail?

explanation.en: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends e-mail from client to server and between mail servers.

stem.en: Which protocol is used to transfer files between computers on a network?

explanation.en: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) uploads and downloads files between a client and an FTP server.

stem.en: Web pages are requested and delivered between a browser and a web server using:

explanation.en: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) works on a request–response model between client (browser) and server.

stem.en: Which protocol establishes a direct connection between two nodes, for example a computer and an ISP over a dial-up line?

explanation.en: PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) connects two nodes directly and supports authentication.

stem.en: In TCP/IP, which statement is correct?

options.en: IP reassembles packets; TCP gives addresses
TCP and IP both only send e-mail
TCP is used only in wireless networks
TCP divides data into packets and reassembles them reliably; IP addresses and routes each packet

explanation.en: TCP ensures reliable, ordered delivery by breaking and reassembling data; IP handles addressing and routing of packets.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Packet switching uses network links more efficiently than circuit switching.
Reason (R): In packet switching no dedicated path is reserved, so links are shared by packets from many users.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: R explains A: shared links are not left idle as in a reserved circuit.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Infrared communication is suitable for linking computers in two different rooms.
Reason (R): Infrared waves cannot pass through walls.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Because infrared cannot pass through walls, it is unsuitable between rooms; A is false and R is true.

stem.en: Which medium is best for the link between the main building and the lab across the valley?

options.en: Coaxial cable laid across the valley
Microwave link between towers with line of sight

explanation.en: Microwaves suit long point-to-point links where cabling is hard; infrared and Bluetooth have very short range.

passage.en: A hill-station hospital must connect its main building to a diagnostic lab 3 km away across a valley, where laying cable is very difficult. Inside the main building, doctors need to share large MRI image files quickly, and the X-ray room has heavy electrical machinery that causes interference. The hospital also wants staff to use tablets anywhere inside the building.

stem.en: Which wired medium suits the X-ray room, where interference is high and large files must move fast?

explanation.en: Optical fibre carries light, so it is immune to electromagnetic interference and offers very high bandwidth.

passage.en: A hill-station hospital must connect its main building to a diagnostic lab 3 km away across a valley, where laying cable is very difficult. Inside the main building, doctors need to share large MRI image files quickly, and the X-ray room has heavy electrical machinery that causes interference. The hospital also wants staff to use tablets anywhere inside the building.

stem.en: How long does it take to transfer a 20 MB file over a link with a data transfer rate of 4 Mbps? (Take 1 byte = 8 bits.)

explanation.en: 20 MB = 20 × 8 = 160 megabits. Time = 160 Mb ÷ 4 Mbps = 40 seconds. 5 seconds forgets to convert bytes to bits.

stem.en:
Match the mode of communication with its example.
(A) Simplex  (B) Half-duplex  (C) Full-duplex
(i) Walkie-talkie
(ii) Telephone call
(iii) Keyboard to computer

explanation.en: A keyboard sends data in one direction only (simplex); a walkie-talkie works both ways but one at a time (half-duplex); a telephone call carries both directions at once (full-duplex).

stem.en: Which wireless medium needs line of sight, works only over a very short distance, cannot pass through walls, and is used in TV remote controls?

explanation.en: Infrared waves (about 300 GHz to 400 THz) work only over short distances in line of sight and are blocked by walls, as in TV remotes. Radio waves pass through walls; microwaves need line of sight but travel long distances.
